title: Opus 5 vs Opus 4.8 — building BurnZone via Kriya
effort: default (Claude Code default, held equal on both arms)
pricing_note: Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 bill at the IDENTICAL $5/$25 per MTok tier. Unlike the Fable lab, no per-token price premium is in play — every cost delta here is pure token volume, driven by Opus 5 running adaptive thinking by default. Costs normalized to official published rates from Claude Code modelUsage telemetry.
headline: Same suite, same keys, same price tier as lab #3. Both models hit the objective ceiling on all four tasks — 2/2 seeded criticals, correct minimal fix, 16/16 rubric, correct VETO — so nothing separates them on the answer key. What separates them is depth past the key and availability: Opus 5 returned ~2.5x the valid defects on the security capture, was the first arm in any lab to pin the no-500 invariant explicitly, and — decisively — never declined. Both security prompts that Fable 5 refused in lab #3 were served by Opus 5 itself, making this the first clean 4/4 head-to-head. It cost 1.94x ($1.88 vs $0.97 across the four tasks), all of it token volume.
